summary: Cheatham County, TN tower at 679 ft; Tennessee Landforms lists it as removed under number 6-9, and no build, staffing or site details were found.

facts.status_note: Removed according to Tennessee Landforms. No source describes what remains at the site today.

evidence.supports: table numbers are state forest tower numbers from a 1976 list, written district-tower
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: numbers tied to the Division of Forestry's 208 tower sites of about 1976
evidence.quote: Division of Forestry (208 tower sites c. 1976, noted in table as distict-tower)

evidence.supports: expansion of TDF as Tennessee Division of Forestry
TDF responsible for 208 towers built about 1930 to 1970
evidence.quote: The TDF was responsible for the construction of 208 fire lookout towers during the period between ca. 1930 and ca. 1970

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, multiple property documentation form
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. Status and number come only from Landforms; the Forest Lookouts page gives the county and nothing else. Sycamore does not appear in the Tennessee Division of Forestry National Register form table, unlike Stony Creek and The Barrens, and the story does not draw a conclusion from that. The record elevation of 207.0 m matches 679 ft. No agency, build year, staffing or photo is sourced.
